patient_context.chief_complaint: A randomized head-to-head trial now directly compared Treatment A and Treatment B. What can be concluded?
patient_context.history: The same target population was randomized to A or B, the same endpoint and follow-up were used, A achieved 62%, B 48%, and the fixture states the prespecified between-group comparison supports superiority of A on that endpoint.

interaction.prompt: Update the comparative conclusion now that direct randomized evidence is available. Keep the conclusion limited to what the head-to-head fixture actually establishes.

must_include: Recognize this as direct randomized head-to-head comparative evidence.
State that the fixture supports Treatment A outperforming Treatment B on the specified endpoint in this trial.
Limit the conclusion to that endpoint/population rather than saying A is universally better in all outcomes and contexts.
must_not_claim: Do not remain in blanket abstention mode and say direct comparison is impossible.
Do not generalize endpoint-specific superiority to every benefit, harm or population.
expected_behavior.uncertainty_behavior: Update decisively on the tested endpoint while preserving external-validity and scope limits.

forbidden_claims: A is better in all respects for every patient
direct superiority still cannot be assessed despite the head-to-head fixture

critical_errors: Fails to update when stronger direct evidence is supplied.
Expands endpoint-specific superiority into a universal superiority claim.
